Emma — thanks for the thoughtful questions. I wanted to give a concise proposal we can iterate on quickly (and save Kurt some back-and-forth with procurement). Below is the approach Redwood recommends and the specific language we can put into the SLA.

1) Baseline uptime: 99.95% monthly availability measured per region\/route as defined in the Agreement (exceptions noted below).

2) Credit model ("service-allowance" approach):
   - Monthly Service Allowance: instead of a single hard cap, we allocate a monthly credit allowance equal to 2% of the invoiced service charges for that billing period (the "service-allowance bucket").
   - Remedy calculation: when monthly availability falls below the baseline, credits are drawn from the allowance proportionally. For example, a 0.05 percentage point breach triggers a proportional draw; larger breaches draw more.
   - Cap and roll-forward: unused allowance rolls forward for up to two billing cycles (so smaller incidents still earn value later), but total credits applied in any single month remain capped at the current allowance plus any rolled-forward amount.

3) Maintenance carveouts and latency treatment:
   - Scheduled maintenance is excluded if notified 72+ hours in advance and performed during the agreed maintenance window.
   - Short, scheduled latency spikes (below 5 minutes per route) are treated as informational and do not trigger credit draws.
   - Emergency maintenance and force majeure events are excluded per standard contract language, but we propose a transparency requirement: redwood will publish a post-event timeline within 48 hours and offer an operational remediation plan for outages >1 hour.

4) Measurement and dispute flow:
   - Redwood provides per-route tokenized metrics (latency percentiles and availability) via the Console and will share the measurement report with the customer within 7 days of month close.
   - Either party can open a dispute within 30 days; interim credits can be escrowed pending final measurement reconciliation.

5) Examples appendix: we'll include a 2-page appendix with 3 worked examples to make the math crystal clear for procurement.

I've attached the same draft with inline annotations and a one-page service-allowance summary for Kurt. If this model sounds reasonable I can have Legal (Laura and Marissa) craft the exact SLA language and redline it into the PDF.

Quick ask: Emma, would Stratos be comfortable with the 2% monthly allowance as a starting point? If your finance team prefers a different percentage, we can make that configurable in the template.

Hi Kurt\/Emma — looping in Legal and Contracts. Appreciate the clear, practical feedback — we can accommodate both asks with a couple of clarifying clauses. Summary of proposed adjustments for the redline: 

• Alternate allowance expression: add a clause that allows the remedy bucket to be elected at signature as either (a) a percentage of monthly invoice (default 2%) or (b) a fixed-dollar amount, with a simple election box on the signature page.

• Latency-only impact: add a narrowly scoped remediation path where the customer may submit a documented user-impact claim (sample telemetry + support ticket correlation). If validated by both parties (measurement reconciliation), a partial draw from the service-allowance bucket may be permitted; any such draw will be pro-rated based on documented impact.

• Measurement transparency: we will include the examples appendix Jonas mentioned and a sample measurement report format.

I've attached a redline that implements the above; it also contains clean language around roll-forward mechanics and the 2-cycle ceiling. Please review the redline and indicate if Stratos prefers the percent or fixed-dollar election. If you confirm, we'll prepare a DocuSign-ready set for countersignature.
